body:
CORRECTION (2026-07-25) — BOTH T45 lenses found this independently: it is NOT only an intra-erase window. TWO LONG-LIVED STATES have the same shape, and our own doctrine blesses both.

1. A tombstone appended DIRECTLY, with no purge ever. authorize runs eraseDefect, which passes an operator-signed, well-shaped tombstone over a live target, and appendImpl only refuses ids that are ALREADY dead. Nothing on that path calls purge. The removal order binds; the bytes stay.
2. An erase() that THROWS at its byte verdict. eraseImpl grounds and flushes the tombstone (erase.ts:283-286), then throws (erase.ts:330-338) if any tier still holds or a pool refused — and deliberately does NOT roll the tombstone back, so a re-run mints no second one.

T70 blesses exactly this in its own header: the bytes leave each tier on that tier own time, and that gap is a HEALTH state rather than a fault — serve keeps serving, status settling. So the divergence below is not a microsecond race. A store can sit in it for as long as the operator leaves it there, with the watch door honoring a removal order that select, freeze and the federation offer do not. A fix aimed at a narrow race would miss the case that actually persists.

DESIGN-STAGE (a new atomicity promise, so it needs Myk's word before code). Found by the T45 build (2026-07-25) while closing in-memory retention, reported rather than quietly widened.

THE WINDOW. `eraseImpl` grounds the tombstone FIRST and purges after — deliberately, so nothing is removed before the record of its removal is durable. But between `append(tombstone)` and `reseat()` there are real `await` yield points: `gw.flush()`, `backend.purge()`, the pool fan-out, `reseat()` itself. Any task that runs in that window sees a store whose ground CONTAINS both the tombstone and its target.

AND THE POINT-READ DOORS DO NOT FILTER THE DEAD SET. `selectImpl`, `Gateway.freeze`, and `offeredDeltasImpl` evaluate over `reactor.snapshot()` with no `readTombstones` consultation. So inside the window: a concurrent `select` returns the condemned delta; a `freeze` mints a ModuleVersion whose members INCLUDE it (and whose content address therefore commits to it — permanently, since a version is a name you ship); a federation pull hands it to a peer, which will then hold it after the local purge completes.

WHY IT IS NOW OBSERVABLE, and this is the sharp part: T45 added a tombstone filter to the WATCH door (`watchImpl`), because that is where the retention lived. So the live door now honors the removal order the instant it is ground, while the point-read doors beside it do not. The asymmetry is a reader-visible divergence between two doors over the same ground at the same moment — exactly the class §24.10 exists to prevent, and the T45 author flagged it rather than papering it.

THE CHOICE (this is what needs deciding, not implementing):
1. A DOOR BARRIER for the duration of the cut — reads that would cross the window wait, the way the T33 living-name lock serializes publishes. Honest and simple to reason about; costs latency on every erase and needs care not to deadlock against the fan-out's own awaits.
2. FILTER THE DEAD SET AT EVERY POINT-READ DOOR — `select`/`freeze`/`offeredDeltas` consult `readTombstones` like the append and federation doors already do. Cheaper, no waiting, and it makes the removal order bind at the same instant everywhere. But it changes what `select` MEANS (it stops being exactly the Term's dset, which §27.6 states and T38's rails pin), and `freeze`'s address would then depend on erasure state — arguably correct, arguably a surprise.
3. DECLARE THE WINDOW as a documented eventual-consistency property, on the record, with `/health` already reporting `settling`. Cheapest; leaves a peer able to acquire a condemned delta seconds before it is purged locally, which is the erasure-evasion shape §24.8 exists to close.

RECOMMENDATION: (2) for `offeredDeltas` (the federation door is where the evasion actually lands, and that door ALREADY filters the dead set on the inbound side — the asymmetry there is arguably a plain bug) plus (1) or (3) for the local read doors, argued on latency. Do NOT adopt (2) for `select` without deciding what it does to §27.6's stated meaning.

RAILS the spec must name: a concurrent `select` landing inside the window (forced with the same injected-hold seam T33 and T64 use, not a timing race) does not return the condemned delta; the same for `freeze` — and assert the ADDRESS, since a version that committed to a condemned member is the permanent artifact; a federation pull inside the window does not hand the peer the delta, asserted at the PEER's resolved reading and not merely at the wire; and the watch door's behavior is unchanged (T45's rails stay green, so the fix cannot be 'make every door as lax as the laxest').

CARE: erasure REACH. Per CLAUDE.md's standing rule (Myk, 2026-07-25), a change that widens what gets purged is Myk's merge and must state in one line what can now be deleted that could not before. This one does not widen the purge — it narrows what is SERVED during a window — but it changes an atomicity promise, so it is his call either way. Related: T44 (pool reach), T62 (one completeness rule), T64 (the slate's own read closure faces the same N-doors problem and its criterion 7 already enumerates them — reconcile rather than duplicate).
title: Erase is not atomic against concurrent readers — the window between tombstone and reseat serves what it has already condemned
